title: Correct canonical binding reader query capacity, disjoint union, and deterministic cutoff tie-breaking
summary: Corrects canonical binding reader query capacity in services/telemetry/ingest_svc.py following genuine FE readiness rejection (Run 38180670594, FE 38183581764 rejected_before_switch at 23:35:24Z with TimeoutError in lifecycle projector bff.strict_health.pre_candidate). Failing-window PostgreSQL canonical binding queries were canceled at 23:35:14, 23:35:21, and 23:35:27Z, and advisory lock canceled at 23:35:19.983Z. Exact blocker PID and full projector traceback were not retained after original compensation, so correlation is distinguished from proven cause, and 172% CPU was recorded at 23:42:00Z after compensation rather than during the 23:35:24Z window. The query capacity is corrected by replacing the previous single GIN OR query with a mutually disjoint dual-branch indexed UNION: branch 1 uses the existing B-tree index idx_telemetry_events_binding_id (payload->>'binding_id' = $1 AND jsonb_typeof(payload->'binding_id') = 'string' AND (payload->>'runtime_binding_id' IS NULL OR (payload->>'runtime_binding_id' = $1 AND jsonb_typeof(payload->'runtime_binding_id') = 'string'))), which exclusively handles all events with binding_id = $1 (including bothalias) while strictly guarding optional runtime_binding_id to be a string type; branch 2 uses GIN index idx_telemetry_events_payload_gin exclusively for sparse runtime_binding_id events where binding_id is absent (payload @> jsonb_build_object('runtime_binding_id', $1::text) AND payload->>'binding_id' IS NULL). This eliminates overlapping bothalias scans and disallows root=$1 in branch 2 (addressing RF6), enforces strict typeguards against numeric and boolean alias types while preserving valid positive string control '99999'. Deterministic cutoff tie-breaking is enforced by ORDER BY created_at DESC, ingested_seq DESC LIMIT ... on both inner branches and outer subquery. On the actual VM repeatable-read READONLY snapshot rb-52 (4.56M estimated rows, 10GB), Root measured: at 00:04:16Z (98cd head) candidate 0.837205s vs original 2.076073s for 50 rows; at 00:24:28Z (533 head) candidate 0.566251s (50 rows) and 0.621517s (100 rows) vs original 2.099816s (50 rows) and 0.339661s (100 rows). Both 50 and 100 return identical event ID sets and same event time multisets, order difference is timestamp ties handled seqDESC, and candidate 50 is exact prefix of 100. Honest documentation: these are sequential point-reads on rb-52 that may warm cache (all original point-reads also executed within the 5s deadline); no causal speedup, cold cache, all bindings, concurrent writer, hosted readiness, or FINAL proof is asserted. Test suite test_14 in services/telemetry/test_main_routes.py seeds 120 valid events and verifies 50/100 cutoffs with genuine equal-created_at ties crossing the 50 and 100 boundaries against an in-memory oracle, limit=200 clamping, positive string control ('owned-positive-string-both'), negative mixed numeric denial ('owned-negative-mixed-numeric'), malformed integer and lowercase/uppercase JSON boolean fail-closed extraction, dualalias conflict negatives, and tenant isolation. Net production lines diff in services/telemetry/ingest_svc.py is exactly +1 line (strictly within <= 10 budget). AC6 is marked pending_delivery until genuine assigned reviewer exact-head review, required 3 CI checks, dev merge by integrator, and native finish.
